texts.value: Extracellular matrix protein (PubMed:22020326, PubMed:28671670, PubMed:28912033). Affects several essential steps in angiogenesis including endothelial cell proliferation, migration, and tube formation (PubMed:22020326, PubMed:28671670, PubMed:28912033). Positively regulates angiogenesis by acting as a ligand for CD93 receptor (PubMed:28671670, PubMed:28912033)

Heteromer of p110, p125, p140 and p200 subunits; disulfide-linked. Interacts with VEGFA. Interacts with CD93; this interaction promotes angiogenesis (PubMed:28671670, PubMed:28912033). Interacts with CD248 (PubMed:28671670)
O-fucosylated within the EMI domain (at Ser-63, Thr-67 and Thr-115) by POFUT3 and POFUT4

Was originally thought to play significant roles in the vascular system and to be required for the maintenance and stability of blood vessels; also thought to be processed by matrix metalloproteinases (MMPs) including MMP9 and, to a lesser degree, by MMP2 upon angiogenic stimulation (PubMed:28435016). However, the corresponding article has been retracted (PubMed:41107108)
